name: Stickman in a 3D world (story)
description: A flat cartoon stickman (big round head, thin limbs, a hat) standing inside a lit real-time 3D diorama: rolling grass, wheat, hills, a barn, a windmill, sun rays, fog. Signs belong to the world. The camera is the star: drone orbit, low tracking, close-ups, top-down, pull-back payoff. Physics or psychology twist stories in 25 to 60 seconds.
rules: The actor is a flat sprite in a lit 3D world: it takes the scene light, casts a projected shadow and always faces the camera.
Text that belongs to the world (signs) is on a prop, never an overlay.
Camera purpose per shot comes from foundation/playbooks/camera.json: hook push-in, establish orbit, reveal whip then hold, emotion extreme close-up, payoff pull-back.
Captions: thin white lowercase, one to three words, y about 68 percent; one yellow word when the line turns.
Day to dusk to night grade across the acts.
camera_language: Wide to show the whole body acting (the silhouette is the performance); medium for talking; close-up on the face for the joke or the reaction. The camera stays low-key: moves are rare and each one is a reveal.
audio_direction: bed, boing/pop on gags, thud on falls
pitfalls: Ball joints stack at the hips in wide poses: keep legs at least 18 degrees apart.
Over-the-shoulder crops the head: acceptable, but keep the hand and the object in the lower two thirds.
High-key lighting hazes distant shots: lower exposure and raise vignette.
